name: veterinary_clinic_system_001_overdue_vaccine_compliance_flag
instruction: Run the daily vaccination compliance snapshot for the practice as of the episode date in veterinary_clinic_system_ops_meta. This mission has three parts, all derived independently from live data. (1) In veterinary_clinic_system_vaccinations, set `compliance_flag` on every row: 'overdue' if its `due_date` is strictly before the episode date, 'due_soon' if its `due_date` falls in [episode_date, episode_date + 7 days] inclusive, and 'current' otherwise. Do not modify any other field on those rows. (2) Cross-check veterinary_clinic_system_reminder_queue: count how many rows with `kind='vaccination_due'` and `status='queued'` are stale because their patient has no overdue or due_soon vaccination as of the episode date. Leave those rows untouched and include only the count in the report. Other `kind` values (invoice_overdue, boarding_checkin) are decoys and must be ignored. (3) Push exactly one row into veterinary_clinic_system_ops_reports with `report='vaccination_compliance_snapshot'` and the live `batch_code`, containing these computed fields: `total_vaccinations` (int), `overdue_count` (int), `due_soon_count` (int), `current_count` (int), `compliance_pct` (round(100 * current_count / total_vaccinations, 1)), `stale_reminder_count` (the count from part 2), `breakdown_by_species` (dict keyed by patient species, each value a dict {overdue, due_soon, current}), and `breakdown_by_location` (dict keyed by location name, each value a dict {overdue, due_soon, current}). The three counts in every breakdown must sum correctly to the species/location totals. If a row with this `report` and `batch_code` already exists from a previous run, overwrite it so the result is idempotent. Do not touch any other collections.

success_criteria.summary: Episode date from ops_meta episode_date, dp() it. Every vaccination row gets the correct compliance_flag and all non-flag fields remain byte-identical to the seed snapshot. The reminder_queue is read but not modified; stale_reminder_count is the number of queued 'vaccination_due' rows whose patient has no overdue or due_soon vaccination. Exactly one ops_reports row (report='vaccination_compliance_snapshot', batch_code) contains the aggregate counts, the rounded compliance percentage, and the species/location breakdowns, all recomputed two independent ways (raw-row Python filter and SQL GROUP BY/COUNT) and matched against what the agent wrote. All collections outside blast_radius are byte-identical to the seed snapshot.

checks.expect: Each row's compliance_flag matches the computed overdue/due_soon/current bucket and all other fields unchanged
Exactly one row per batch_code for report='vaccination_compliance_snapshot' with all required fields and correct aggregate values
Every aggregate total/overdue/due_soon/current count and every species/location breakdown agrees between a raw-row Python filter and an independent SQL GROUP BY/COUNT query

hazards: Decoy reminder_queue rows: the seed snapshot has exactly 4 reminder_queue rows — 2 with kind='vaccination_due' status='queued' (patient 2 due 2026-08-14 and patient 5 due 2026-09-10), 1 invoice_overdue, and 1 boarding_checkin. The non-vaccination kinds and the queued vax rows that remain valid must not be modified, deleted, or counted as stale.

Date-boundary precision: at the default episode date 2026-09-30 there are 122 overdue and 16 due_soon vaccinations, and 20 due dates fall in the jitter-sensitive band [2026-09-27, 2026-10-07]. The overdue check must be strict '<', the due_soon window must be inclusive of both endpoints, and the episode date jitters ±3 days in env.py around a base anchor.

Multi-hop join and collision hazards: 300 patients map to 5 species and 3 locations, and the 50-name pet-name pool means names can repeat. A solution that groups by row-level text or uses the wrong join path (e.g. ignoring patient) will produce wrong breakdown_by_species and breakdown_by_location; the correct keys are patients.species and locations.name via patients.location_id.

Idempotency on re-run: all 600 vaccinations already carry compliance_flag after the first run and the ops_reports row for this batch_code already exists. A second run must update the same flags to the same values, keep reminder_queue untouched, and overwrite (not duplicate) the ops_reports summary.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Upgrades a single-row flagging task into a multi-collection, multi-hop aggregation and reconciliation mission: every vaccination row is classified by a per-episode business-date window, the result is cross-checked against the live reminder_queue without modifying it, and a single report with species/location breakdowns is verified via dual raw-row and SQL paths.
